brief: Funding fears in October capex deals pulled capital into credit yields and away from elevated Tech equity exposure, broadening the market as SPX equal weight outperformed SPX by about 6%. Hyperscaler earnings did not reverse the rotation: although results reinforced AI demand, mounting capex deployment and pressure on ROI/FCF meant no hyperscaler closed positive after reporting, even erasing ORCL's mid-week +10% rally by Friday; the cumulative misses forced long selling in top SPY/QQQ weights through key technical levels, and UBS expects a retest of Friday's lows Monday with sizable systematic selling. Still, UBS views hyperscalers as the higher-quality AI holding given a capital-constrained backdrop, with the question being when investors re-add given existing length into the prints. Midterms could be a risk circuit breaker this week, but UBS doubts sustained upside without long-only sponsorship. Healthcare (XLV) is the rotation's winner, up 23% in H2 with half the gain in October alone, on defensive and AI/longevity growth appeal. Separately, UBS Economics expects Fed funds pricing to stay subdued (no full hike priced until Jan'27) even as Q3 GDP holds at 3.4% and October payrolls print near 65K.
